doc: I85 (= I39a) sidecar, fixed at the I85 prereg (contract: the docstring of tests_m3/test_derivation_extraction.py). It is the only place the target vocabulary of holon/derivation lives: the consumer's entry and its batch parameter, the join function, the environment boundary of the consumer (the functions answered by the real library, with their result kinds), the corpus compressor, the product machine's wiring (the Rollup document's commit action, its parameter, the committed-header family, the batch type and its blob field, the deployment record, I20's genesis header, the actors and the answers of the commit's external calls) and the corpus (rule C1, generated by tests_m3/_i85.py::corpus). It states no outcome.

compressor.text: The DA codec's zstd compressor (the submitter's side), run by the real library to turn a raw corpus payload into the bytes packed into blobs (rule C2).

(*github.com/morph-l2/go-ethereum/core/t.text: MarshalBinary() of a transaction the oracle decoded: its encoding as the oracle reported it, and a nil error.

(github.com/morph-l2/go-ethereum/core/ty.text: Transactions.Len() is len(s) of the slice.

github.com/morph-l2/morph-da-codec/bindi.text: The DA codec's zstd decompressor (cgo over a Rust static library, a magic-less zstd frame): its output bytes or its error. It is the decompression half of the compression hypothesis I38 states (HypZ); the consumer reaches it through morph-l2/common/codec/zstd.DecompressBatchBytes, which is extracted.

morph-l2/common/batch.DecodeTxsFromBytes.text: The batch payload's transaction-stream decoder: the transactions it decodes, each as its binary encoding (MarshalBinary), whether the list is nil, or its error. Its body is in the extracted package common/batch, but it decodes through go-ethereum's RLP and typed-transaction codecs; the boundary is named here, so the stream's own rules (a zero type byte ends it, its size checks) are the real library's, not the model's.

product.text: The product machine's Solidity half is the adopted Rollup document's commit action evaluated by holon.extracted_eval from the Rollup's storage in I80's deployment record (I20's deployment); the actors are I20's submitters who 2 and 3 (I20's submitter stand-in answers isActive true for both); the queue holds no message, so it answers its first unfinalized enqueue time with the block's timestamp (L1MessageQueueWithGasPriceOracle at the head) and no commit carries an L1 message. A blob's hash is a stand-in (0x01, then bytes 1..31 of the blob's sha256), not its KZG versioned hash: the derivation reads no hash, and the Rollup treats blob hashes as words.
